minutes.headline: Assessors are drafting a new senior means-tested tax exemption/deferral program; not yet adopted.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors spent most of this meeting line-editing draft brochures and application forms for a new senior means-tested property tax exemption and deferral program, working through eligibility rules, income limits, and cost estimates, with no vote to adopt yet. It also heard the principal assessor's status report on abatements, the cyclical inspection program, and a Clause 41D/17 exemption amendment that was moved forward as amended by town counsel, before entering executive session on abatement/exemption matters.

votes.motion: Motion to approve the minutes for release
Motion to proceed with the Clause 41D/17 exemption changes as amended by Town Council
Motion to adjourn open meeting and enter executive session (purpose 7, abatement/exemption applications), not to return to open session

budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor reported nearly all abatement applications were complete, with a handful still awaiting information ahead of executive-session review.
The board discussed hiring outside expertise for technical valuation work, noting money exists in the capital plan for next year to fund it.

budget_items.topic: Senior population count for exemption planning
budget_items.what_was_said: The assessor requested from a town contact the number of residents 65 and older to help estimate how many applicants a new senior exemption might draw.

budget_items.topic: Median sale price threshold for senior exemption
budget_items.what_was_said: The board debated whether to use last year's classification-hearing figure or the vision system's more recent median assessed price as the exemption's value restriction.

budget_items.topic: 1% levy cap calculation for exemption program
budget_items.what_was_said: The assessor calculated the program's cost as 1% of last year's levy, dividing it by the circuit breaker maximum to estimate how many applicants could be funded at the maximum benefit.
The board raised an unresolved question about what exemption share to grant an applicant who owns only a partial interest in a property held in trust.

budget_items.topic: Income limits for senior circuit breaker exemption
budget_items.what_was_said: The board corrected the draft brochure's stated income cap, noting the circuit-breaker income limits differ by filing status and need to be verified against the guide.
The board discussed that state law limits the circuit-breaker-linked exemption to a one-acre valuation, and the property record card would need to reflect that limit.

budget_items.topic: Deferred property tax example figures in brochure
budget_items.what_was_said: The board edited illustrative example figures in the deferral brochure showing how deferred property tax and interest would accumulate over 15 years before repayment.
The assessor described current office staffing while making the case for additional help, citing the town's total valuation and current admin hours.
The office reported needing to complete about 500 cyclical inspections by the end of June out of roughly 5,200 parcels town-wide, and acknowledged the pace is tight.
The assessor characterized the fiscal impact of restoring two applicants to Clause 41D/17 status as negligible when spread across town parcels, with no effect on state reimbursement.

decisions.decision: Board policies document review held over to next meeting since it had not yet been reviewed.
Board leaned toward requiring only the state (not federal) income tax return on the senior exemption application, with a final recommendation due next meeting.
Application documents will be prefixed and numbered separately (e.g., circuit-breaker vs. deferral materials) to distinguish which packet each page belongs to.
Assessor will investigate removing the specific year from the senior exemption application/brochure so it does not need reprinting every year.
Board will target the end of April as the informal deadline for completing the preliminary deferral agreement with the pending applicant.
Detailed review of the organizational workload/staffing metrics document deferred to the next meeting for a fuller conversation.
Board decided not to reach out to the Department of Revenue in advance about the Clause 41D/17 baseline-reset question, choosing to proceed and address any pushback if it comes.

what_happened.line: Assessors kept drafting a new senior means-tested property tax exemption and deferral program, with no vote to adopt it yet.
The board moved forward a Clause 41D/17 exemption amendment as revised by town counsel, restoring two applicants' exemption status.
Eligibility questions -- partial trust ownership, which tax return to require, the acreage cap under Clause 41A -- remain unresolved and go to the next meeting.
The assessor's office reported it is behind pace on its cyclical inspection program, needing about 500 more inspections by end of June.
The board deferred review of its own policies document and of staffing/workload metrics for the assessor's office to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: A new senior tax exemption and deferral program is still being written, not yet in effect -- residents who may qualify cannot apply until the board adopts final eligibility rules and a levy-impact estimate.
The Clause 41D/17 change affects how two specific applicants' exemptions are calculated and was advanced without a Department of Revenue check in advance, per the board's own choice.
The inspection program's pace, and the assessor's push for added staffing, affect how quickly property valuations townwide are updated and reviewed.
